answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by requiring every new identity to lock a modest stake of tokens for a fixed number of epochs before it can earn. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents would therefore have to immobilize a large capital ridge of value for weeks, turning the scheme into an expensive fable while the real juniper of honest participation slowly grows its roots and rewards. This cost scales linearly with the number of sybils and is forfeited on detection of coordinated fraud.
